scope: V2 SystemBackup disabled-policy resource bundle and attached-volume SystemRestore refusal qualification only; not actual detached restore, absent-volume reconstruction, DR or complete LONGHORN-48
conclusions: Default target stores a resource ZIP plus JSON cfg; Config.Checksum is the complete ZIP SHA256. The archive includes metadata.yaml and native YAML lists under the SystemBackup name prefix.

metadata.yaml is encoded by manager util.EncodeToYAMLFile using gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.4.0; systemBackupMeta has json tags only, so keys are lowercase Go field names (longhornnamespaceuuid, not the JSON misspelling longhornNamspaceUUID). Resource YAML lists use Kubernetes printers.YAMLPrinter separately and retain native JSON schema.

Pinned bundle includes BackupTargets as well as documented resources, but no Secret, Pod or Node lists. It is not a full Kubernetes backup. Backup target credentials and node/disk admission must exist independently.
Resource-only disabled policy does not create volume data backups. Read every existing referenced volume backup object independently; Ready alone does not prove data recovery.

Missing non-standby volumes are recreated using LastBackup recorded in the bundled Volume.status; a later backup appearing in the store does not automatically replace this recorded source. Existing Volume/PV/PVC are not rolled back.

Restore requires all volumes detached. Deleting a SystemRestore aborts remaining rollout through its owning Job cleanup; completed steps are not transactionally rolled back. Exact recovery semantics require their own integration gate.

The source qualification may validate cfg/ZIP, original namespace/Volume/PV/PVC/SC UIDs, expected LastBackup, exact attached-volume refusal and source cross-node readback. It cannot stand in for actual detached SystemRestore, absent-volume reconstruction, independent DR or final delivery PASS.
classification: test-gate integration using existing config+kubecli requests; no new production API
checksum_correction: GetFileChecksum uses sha256.New, unlike the truncated SHA512 GetChecksum for block content. Corrects prior source interpretation; historical first-failure logs remain unchanged.
